entries.meaning: marks an event or new situation

explanations.title: 人 (rén)
explanations.summary: Can refer to a person or to people; the character itself does not mark singular or plural. 三个人 means three people.

explanations.title: 大 (dà)
explanations.summary: Describes something big or large. In a simple description say 很大, rather than inserting 是 before 大.

explanations.title: 一 (yī)
explanations.summary: Yī is the dictionary reading and is used in counting. Before a fourth tone it normally becomes yí; before a first, second, or third tone it normally becomes yì.

explanations.title: 二 (èr)
explanations.summary: Use 二 when counting or reading digits. Before most classifiers, 两 is normally used instead: 两个人 means two people.

explanations.title: 三 (sān)
explanations.summary: First tone: high and level. 三个人 means three people.

explanations.title: 日 (rì)
explanations.summary: A character used for sun or day, especially in compounds and written dates. For the sun in ordinary conversation, 太阳 is usual; 天 is common when counting days.

explanations.title: 月 (yuè)
explanations.summary: In dates, a number plus 月 names the month: 三月 is March. 月 also means moon; everyday speech often uses 月亮 for the moon.

explanations.title: 水 (shuǐ)
explanations.summary: 喝水 means drink water. The final ui is written with the tone mark on i: shuǐ.

explanations.title: 木 (mù)
explanations.summary: A character meaning wood or tree, often used inside compounds. 树 is the usual everyday word for a tree.

explanations.title: 天 (tiān)
explanations.summary: Can mean day or sky. 三天 means three days; 今天 means today.

explanations.title: 我 (wǒ)
explanations.summary: Use 我 for yourself. Chinese pronouns do not change form between I and me.

explanations.title: 你 (nǐ)
explanations.summary: The usual singular you. 您 (nín) is a more respectful form.

explanations.title: 他 (tā)
explanations.summary: Written 他 refers to he or him. It sounds exactly like 她 (she/her), so speech needs context.

explanations.title: 她 (tā)
explanations.summary: Written 她 refers to she or her. It sounds exactly like 他 (he/him); the 女 component helps distinguish the writing.

explanations.title: 是 (shì)
explanations.summary: Links a person or thing to an identity or category: 我是学生 means I am a student. It is not a general equivalent of English yes or the is before an adjective.

explanations.title: 五 (wǔ)
explanations.summary: Third tone. In ordinary speech a third tone is often low rather than a full dip and rise.

explanations.title: 八 (bā)
explanations.summary: First tone. 八个人 means eight people.

explanations.title: 十 (shí)
explanations.summary: 十一 means eleven and 二十 means twenty. 十 and 石 (stone) are pronounced alike.

explanations.title: 上 (shàng)
explanations.summary: Can mean above or up. It also has other uses in phrases such as 上学, go to school.

explanations.title: 下 (xià)
explanations.summary: Can mean below or down. It also has other uses, so the whole phrase determines the meaning.

explanations.title: 目 (mù)
explanations.summary: A character meaning eye, mostly used in compounds. The ordinary conversational word for eye is 眼睛 (yǎnjing). 目 and 木 sound alike.

explanations.title: 石 (shí)
explanations.summary: A character meaning stone, commonly used in compounds. 石头 (shítou) is an everyday word for a stone. 石 also has another reading in a traditional unit of measure.

explanations.title: 家 (jiā)
explanations.summary: Can mean home or family. 回家 means return home; 家 does not only refer to the physical building.

explanations.title: 谢谢 (xièxie)
explanations.summary: Use to thank someone. The second syllable is neutral and usually shorter and lighter than the first.

explanations.title: 朋友 (péngyou)
explanations.summary: An everyday word for friend. The second syllable, you, is neutral: péngyou.

explanations.title: 今天 (jīntiān)
explanations.summary: Both syllables have first tone. 今天 is today, 昨天 yesterday, and 明天 tomorrow.

explanations.title: 学校 (xuéxiào)
explanations.summary: A place of education. The tones are second then fourth.

explanations.title: 喜欢 (xǐhuan)
explanations.summary: Can be followed by a noun or an activity: 喜欢茶 means like tea; 喜欢看书 means like reading. The second syllable, huan, is neutral.

explanations.title: 妈妈 (māma)
explanations.summary: An everyday word for mother. The first syllable has first tone and the second is neutral.

explanations.title: 看 (kàn)
explanations.summary: Use kàn for looking, watching, or reading. 看书 means read a book. 看 also has the reading kān for guarding or looking after.

explanations.title: 吗 (ma)
explanations.summary: At the end of a statement, 吗 makes a yes/no question. This particle is neutral tone; do not add it automatically to questions already containing 什么 or 谁.

explanations.title: 的 (de)
explanations.summary: Links an owner or description to a noun: 我的书 means my book. This grammatical use is neutral de; the character has other readings in other words.

explanations.title: 很 (hěn)
explanations.summary: Often comes before an adjective. In an ordinary description it may simply make the sentence natural, without strongly emphasizing very.

explanations.title: 叫 (jiào)
explanations.summary: Use 我叫... to give your name. 叫 also means to call or shout in other contexts.

explanations.title: 名字 (míngzi)
explanations.summary: Means a person's or thing's name. The second syllable, zi, is neutral.

explanations.title: 什么 (shénme)
explanations.summary: Use to ask what something is or what someone does or wants. The second syllable, me, is neutral. 什么 stays where the answer would go in the sentence.

explanations.title: 个 (gè)
explanations.summary: A common counting word between a number and a noun: 三个人 means three people. Its dictionary tone is fourth; it is often neutral in phrases such as 一个 (yí ge).

explanations.title: 两 (liǎng)
explanations.summary: Normally used before classifiers: 两个人 means two people. Use 二 for counting one, two, three and for most digit-by-digit numbers.

explanations.title: 有 (yǒu)
explanations.summary: Expresses possession or existence. 我有书 means I have a book or books. Its usual negative is 没有, not 不有.

explanations.title: 哥哥 (gēge)
explanations.summary: Refers to an older brother. Chinese distinguishes older and younger siblings; the second syllable is neutral.

explanations.title: 孩子 (háizi)
explanations.summary: The usual everyday word for a child or children. The second syllable is neutral; 子 alone is not the ordinary conversational substitute.

explanations.title: 想 (xiǎng)
explanations.summary: Before an action, 想 can express wanting to do it. 想喝茶 means want to drink tea. It can also mean think or miss someone.

explanations.title: 喝 (hē)
explanations.summary: Use with drinks: 喝水 means drink water. The reading taught here is hē; 喝 has another reading in other uses.

explanations.title: 茶 (chá)
explanations.summary: 喝茶 means drink tea. 茶 has a rising second tone.

explanations.title: 去 (qù)
explanations.summary: Use before a destination: 去学校 means go to school. Compare 来, come.

explanations.title: 回 (huí)
explanations.summary: 回家 means return home. 回 can also mean reply in other contexts.

explanations.title: 在 (zài)
explanations.summary: Use to give a location: 我在家 means I am at home. Before an action, 在 can also mark that it is in progress.

explanations.title: 明天 (míngtiān)
explanations.summary: The day after today. 明 has second tone and 天 has first tone.

explanations.title: 现在 (xiànzài)
explanations.summary: Refers to the present time. Both syllables have fourth tone.

explanations.title: 时候 (shíhou)
explanations.summary: Used in 什么时候 (shénme shíhou), meaning when. It is not the word for an hour; hou is neutral.

explanations.title: 星期 (xīngqī)
explanations.summary: 星期一 through 星期六 name Monday through Saturday. Sunday is 星期日 or 星期天.

explanations.title: 点 (diǎn)
explanations.summary: After a number, 点 gives the hour: 三点 means three o'clock. It has several other meanings, including point or dot.

explanations.title: 忙 (máng)
explanations.summary: 我很忙 means I am busy. 很 can make a simple description natural without strongly emphasizing very.

explanations.title: 学生 (xuésheng)
explanations.summary: Student. CC-CEDICT records xuésheng with neutral sheng; the official 2025 HSK syllabus gives xuéshēng. Both are accepted here. Do not confuse 学生 with 老师 (teacher).

explanations.title: 学习 (xuéxí)
explanations.summary: Used for learning or studying. 学习汉语 means study Chinese.

explanations.title: 汉语 (hànyǔ)
explanations.summary: Refers to the Chinese language. In this course the spoken variety taught is standard Mandarin; 中文 is another common term for Chinese.

explanations.title: 书 (shū)
explanations.summary: An everyday word for book. 看书 means read a book; use 本 as the classifier when counting books.

explanations.title: 这 (zhè)
explanations.summary: Points to something nearby or being discussed. Compare 那, that. Before classifiers you may also hear zhèi.

explanations.title: 钱 (qián)
explanations.summary: An everyday word for money. 多少钱 means how much money or how much does it cost.

explanations.title: 多少 (duōshao)
explanations.summary: Asks about an amount or number. 多少钱 asks the price. The second syllable, shao, is neutral in this question word as taught here.
